interface.name: treeland_dde_shell_manager_v1
interface.description: This interface allows DDE to configure some treeland functions.

request.name: get_window_overlap_checker
request.description: Create a treeland_window_overlap_checker object.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: the new window overlap checker object

request.name: get_shell_surface

description.summary: create a shell surface from a surface

request.description:
Create a shell surface for an existing wl_surface.
Only one shell surface can be associated with a given surface.
Recommended for use with xdg_surface.

arg.name: surface
arg.summary: the surface to create a shell surface for

request.name: get_treeland_dde_active
request.description: Create a new dde active for a given seat.

request.name: get_treeland_multitaskview
request.description: Create a new multitaskview context for toggle.

request.name: get_treeland_window_picker
request.description: Create a new window picker to pick window.

request.name: get_treeland_lockscreen
request.description: Create a new lockscreen context for toggle.

request.name: set_xwindow_position_relative

description.summary: Move a XWayland surface to a position relative to a wl_surface

request.description:
Move the top-left point of a XWayland surface specified with Window ID, to a position that has (dx, dy) offset from the top-left point of a wl_surface
Once the server finished process it send "done" to the callback. The callback data 0 means no error occured, 1 means something went wrong and the move cannot be done.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the treeland_dde_shell_manager_v1 object.

interface.name: treeland_window_overlap_checker
interface.description: A treeland_window_overlap_checker object monitors whether the detected window region overlaps with xdg-shell toplevels.

event.name: enter
event.description: Sent when the detected window region begins to overlap with any xdg-shell toplevel. Sent at most once per update cycle.

event.name: leave

description.summary: detected window is no longer overlapped

event.description: Sent when the detected window region no longer overlaps with any xdg-shell toplevel. Sent at most once per update cycle.

entry.name: top
entry.summary: the top edge of the anchor rectangle

entry.name: bottom
entry.summary: the bottom edge of the anchor rectangle

entry.name: left
entry.summary: the left edge of the anchor rectangle

entry.name: right
entry.summary: the right edge of the anchor rectangle

request.name: update
request.description: This interface is used to receive the detected surface. When the xdgshell window in the workspace overlaps with the detected window, an event will be sent to notify the client to process it. The window position will only be recorded when this interface is called. If the window moves, this interface needs to be called again.

arg.name: width
arg.summary: width of the detected window region

arg.name: height
arg.summary: height of the detected window region

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroys the treeland_window_overlap_checker object.
Send this request when the client no longer needs overlap notifications from this object.

interface.name: treeland_dde_shell_surface_v1
interface.description:
An interface that may be implemented by a wl_surface, for implementations that provide the shell user interface.
It provides requests to set surface role, set skip, set the position set auto placement in output coordinates.
On the server side the object is automatically destroyed when the related wl_surface is destroyed. On client side, treeland_dde_shell_surface_v1.destroy() must be called before destroying the wl_surface object.

request.name: destroy
request.description:
The treeland_dde_shell_surface_v1 interface is removed from the wl_surface object that was turned into a shell surface with the treeland_dde_shell_manager_v1.get_shell_surface request.
The shell surface role is lost and wl_surface is unmapped.

request.name: set_surface_position
request.description:
Move the surface to new coordinates.
Coordinates are global, for example 50,50 for a 1920,0+1920x1080 output is 1970,50 in global coordinates space.

enum.name: role
enum.description:
These values indicate which roles a surface can be rendered in, They are ordered by z depth.
Displayed below wlr-layer-shell, at the overlay level of the workspace.
Multiple surfaces can share a single role, and ordering within a single role is undefined.

request.name: set_role

description.summary: assign a role to this surface

request.description: Assign a role to a shell surface.

request.name: set_auto_placement

description.summary: Place the surface at the bottom of the cursor area

request.description:
Set the vertical alignment of the surface within the cursor width.
Do not use it together with set_surface_position to avoid exceptions.
The position of the surface will be controlled by the compositor after the request, including preventing it from being displayed beyond the edge of the output.

arg.name: y_offset
arg.summary: y position is relative to the cursor bottom

request.name: set_skip_switcher

description.summary: make the window not appear in a switcher

request.description: Setting this bit will indicate that the window prefers not to be listed in a switcher.

arg.name: skip
arg.summary: Boolean value that sets whether to skip the window switcher.

request.name: set_skip_dock_preview

description.summary: make the window not appear in a dock preview

request.description: Setting this bit will indicate that the window prefers not to be listed in a dock preview.

arg.name: skip
arg.summary: Boolean value that sets whether to skip the dock preview.

request.name: set_skip_muti_task_view

description.summary: make the window not appear in a mutitask view

request.description: Setting this bit will indicate that the window prefers not to be listed in a mutitask view.

arg.name: skip
arg.summary: Boolean value that sets whether to skip the mutitask view.

request.name: set_accept_keyboard_focus

description.summary: control whether the surface accepts keyboard focus

request.description: Setting this will determine whether the surface can receive keyboard focus. When set to 0, the surface will not receive keyboard focus even when clicked or activated. When set to 1 (default), the surface will receive keyboard focus normally.

arg.name: accept
arg.summary: Boolean value that sets whether to accept keyboard focus
